definitions.explanation: A condition of high moisture in the air. Often used to describe climate or weather conditions.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{夏|なつ}は{高温|こうおん}{多湿|たしつ}だ。
examples.english: Japanese summers are hot and humid.

examples.japanese: {多湿|たしつ}な{環境|かんきょう}ではカビが{生|は}えやすい。
examples.english: Mold grows easily in humid environments.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{一年中|いちねんじゅう}{多湿|たしつ}で、{除湿機|じょしつき}が{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: This area is humid year-round, so a dehumidifier is essential.

notes:
{多湿|たしつ} combines {多|た} (much, many) and {湿|しつ} (moisture, humidity).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高温|こうおん}{多湿|たしつ} (hot and humid — the most common collocation)
- {多湿|たしつ}な{環境|かんきょう} (humid environment)
- {多湿|たしつ}な{気候|きこう} (humid climate)

USAGE:
Most frequently appears in the set phrase {高温|こうおん}{多湿|たしつ} to describe the characteristic summer climate of Japan. The antonym is {乾燥|かんそう} (dry).
